transcript:
user: What is the difference between READ COMMITTED and SERIALIZABLE?
assistant: READ COMMITTED sees rows committed before each statement, so two statements in one transaction can see different data. SERIALIZABLE behaves as if transactions ran one at a time, at the cost of serialization failures you must retry.
user: So SERIALIZABLE can fail?
assistant: Yes — it aborts transactions that would break serializability, and the application is expected to retry them.
required_points: READ COMMITTED can see different data between statements
SERIALIZABLE behaves as if transactions ran one at a time
SERIALIZABLE can abort transactions that must be retried
forbidden_claims: SERIALIZABLE is always the better choice
notes: Three points where the third is a consequence the user had to ask for. A summary that stops at the definitions loses the operational cost.
